trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any credible OpenAI IPO/valuation headline or S-1 filing rumor is driving the probability move; without a news catalyst treat as noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare MSFT and NVDA intraday moves to broad Nasdaq (QQQ) to see if any AI-complex idiosyncratic move exists beyond beta.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether the Polymarket shift is liquidity-driven (thin book) versus informed; check volume.
time_plan.6h: Look for confirmation across multiple OpenAI-related markets (IPO-by-date, valuation brackets) for internal consistency.
time_plan.12h: Close out research view; record whether MSFT/AI-complex showed any move attributable to OpenAI valuation news versus none (expected).

predictions.reasoning: OpenAI is private with no announced IPO; this market resolves on a specific market-cap bracket ($1.25T-$1.5T) at some future first trading day through end-2026. A shift in the implied probability of a narrow valuation bracket carries almost no clean, tradable information for any listed asset over a 12h window. The closest fundamental link is Microsoft, which holds a large stake in OpenAI and would mechanically benefit from a higher OpenAI valuation. But (a) the timing is long-dated and conditional on an IPO that may not occur, (b) a bracket-specific probability move is directionally ambiguous — probability can rise because the market expects a valuation to land IN this band (implying it is NOT the higher $1.5T+ outcome), so it is not even monotonic in 'OpenAI worth more.' Mapping is too weak to assign a direction.

evidence_used: Market question concerns OpenAI IPO-day market cap in a specific $1.25T-$1.5T bracket
Resolution allows 'No IPO by December 31, 2026' — event is conditional and long-dated
OpenAI is a private company; Microsoft is its largest strategic investor/partner
No announced IPO date or S-1 as of the market's framing
uncertainty_notes: Bracket-specific probability is non-monotonic in OpenAI valuation, so even a large probability move has ambiguous asset direction
Event horizon extends to end-2026, far beyond the 12h prediction window
No liquid instrument directly tracks OpenAI's private valuation
Polymarket book for this question is likely thin, making probability moves noisy

llm_justification.summary: This prediction market asks whether OpenAI's IPO-day market cap lands in a narrow $1.25T-$1.5T bracket, conditional on an IPO happening by end-2026. There is no clean, liquid public-market proxy: OpenAI is private, the event is long-dated and conditional, and a bracket-specific probability move is directionally ambiguous. The only fundamental link is Microsoft's stake, but the mapping is far too weak and slow-moving to produce a tradable 12h signal. Direction is unclear, confidence is low, and the expected move is well below the 700bps tradable threshold.
key_assumptions: No imminent OpenAI IPO news catalyst is present
Microsoft is the closest liquid exposure to OpenAI valuation
Polymarket probability moves here are largely noise/liquidity rather than leaked information
failure_modes: A genuine OpenAI IPO/valuation leak could move MSFT and the AI complex meaningfully, which this 'unclear/low' call would miss
The bracket structure means probability can move for reasons opposite to a naive 'higher valuation' read
MSFT is a weak proxy — its market cap dwarfs the OpenAI stake, diluting any signal
The event may never occur (resolves 'No IPO'), making the entire mapping moot
